title: converge-presubmit-metadata-index-and-introduce-dep-freshness-prober
author: Aditi Rao
body:
Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit metadata index to make presubmit selection deterministic and adds a Dep Freshness Prober that surfaces stale transitive dev-deps and flagged security-sensitive transitive upgrades. Motivation: The monolithic presubmit selector has drifted and causes noisy CI runs and unnecessary long-running lint shards. We want a small, index-based mapper that can cheaply determine which presubmit profiles to run given changed file paths, and a separate verifier that checks dependency freshness and flags potential regression windows before CI runs expensive integration tests. This reduces CI load and gives faster feedback to authors for dependency issues.

What changed (single continuous description): Added a new presubmit-mapper service that builds and ships a compact metadata index (sources/redwood/ci/presubmit_index/*.json.tmpl and a generator at sources/github/redwood/ci/presubmit_index/generate_index.go). The index maps glob patterns to typed lint/test profiles. Introduced a Dep Freshness Prober (sources/github/redwood/ci/dep_prober/) that integrates with the dep snapshot service and runs lightweight semantic checks against the lockfiles to emit a pass/warn/fail signal. Hooked both into the presubmit bootstrap path so the index is consulted before lint/test matrix expansion and the Dep Prober runs as a pre-check gate. Small ergonomic changes: added CLI flags to local devcontainer runner to emulate index behavior and a dev mode for the prober. Updated docs: docs/ci/presubmit-mapper.md and docs/ci/dep-prober.md.

Commits (high level): 1) Add presubmit index generator and templates (generate_index.go, schema v1). 2) Implement presubmit-mapper lookup logic and unit tests. 3) Add dep-prober core checkers and lockfile parsers. 4) Wire prober into CI bootstrap and add fail-fast config. 5) Docs, examples, and devcontainer flags.

Files changed (high level list): sources/github/redwood/ci/presubmit_index/generate_index.go, sources/github/redwood/ci/presubmit_index/templates/*.tmpl, sources/github/redwood/ci/mapper/mapper.go, sources/github/redwood/ci/mapper/mapper_test.go, sources/github/redwood/ci/dep_prober/prober.go, sources/github/redwood/ci/dep_prober/checks/*.go, sources/github/redwood/ci/dep_prober/readme.md, docs/ci/presubmit-mapper.md, docs/ci/dep-prober.md, .github/workflows/presubmit-bootstrap.yml, tools/devcontainer/README.md, scripts/ci/prime-presubmit-cache.sh

Behavioral notes: The presubmit index is generated during our presubmit-cache job and stored as an artifact that the presubmit-bootstrap runner downloads. The mapper uses ordered pattern matching with explicit precedence annotations in the index so behavior is deterministic across runtimes. The Dep Freshness Prober is intentionally conservative: it will only fail the presubmit if a transitive dev-dep has a known-critical advisory or if a transitive upgrade would change major semver boundaries for a package we mark as sensitive. Otherwise it surfaces warnings in the PR checks.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for mapper logic and prober checkers. Updated GitHub workflow presubmit-bootstrap.yml to run the prober as a lightweight pre-check (timeout 3m). CI matrix change: split heavy integration tests to run only when presubmit-mapper indicates backend/core code change. The PR CI artifacts show: initial run failed on lint in mapper_test (style) -> author fixed; second run passed all checks (unit, lint, presubmit-bootstrap). See CI table below in this body.

CI checks (summary inline): presubmit-bootstrap: pass (prober ran, index downloaded), unit-tests: pass, lint: pass (one autofix), integration-smoke: skipped for docs-only path, security-scan: pass, license-check: pass.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind a feature-flag controlled by an environment variable PRESUBMIT_INDEX_ENABLED=false by default. 2) Enable for 25% of PRs for 48h, monitor presubmit-run-time and cache hit rate. 3) If metrics look good, flip default to true and remove feature flag in a follow-up cleanup PR. 4) Dep Prober initially set to warn-only; after 2 weeks of signal and team calibration, escalate to fail for critical advisories.

Review conversation (highlights): Liam Carter: "Nice—index approach should reduce CI fanout. Please ensure precedence rules are documented and add a deterministic tie-breaker." Author (Aditi Rao): "Added 'precedence' key and deterministic fallback in generate_index.go; documented behavior in presubmit-mapper.md." Sofia Martinez: "Dep-prober lockfile parser duplicates some logic from dep-snapshot service. Can we reuse utilities?" Author: "Refactored to import dep-snapshot utils and added wrapper adapters to keep prober hermetic for e2e tests." Darren Kim: "CI changes look good; consider a short circuit for docs-only PRs earlier in the pipeline." Author: "Added an early docs-only quick-exit in presubmit-bootstrap.yml and updated docs to show local dev behavior"

Related items and tickets: ENG-2045 (presubmit inefficiency), ENG-2110 (dep observability), also references a Linear task PM-18 for release notes.

Release notes (for internal changelog): - Introduce presubmit metadata index and mapper for deterministic presubmit selection. - Add Dep Freshness Prober to surface stale or security-sensitive transitive dependency changes before heavy CI runs. - Update presubmit bootstrap workflow to consult index and run prober as a pre-check.

Manual test steps for reviewers: 1) Run make presubmit-index locally (requires go1.20) and inspect generated index under _build/presubmit_index.json. 2) In devcontainer, run ./tools/devcontainer/run-presubmit --use-index --prober-mode=warn to simulate CI. 3) Create a sample PR that only touches docs/ and verify presubmit quickly exits with skipped heavy tests.

Backward compatibility and breaking changes: None expected. The presubmit bootstrap keeps legacy selector as fallback when PRESUBMIT_INDEX_ENABLED=false. The new prober only warns by default.

Post-merge housekeeping tasks: 1) Schedule feature flag ramp (follow-up issue ENG-2199). 2) Add telemetry to CI to record index hit rates and prober warn/fail rates (ticket ENG-2200). 3) If stable after two weeks, remove feature flag and simplify bootstrap.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2025-11-06 after approvals from Liam Carter and Sofia Martinez and green CI.

Notes: This PR aims to be incremental and low-risk — index is compact, generated artifact is language-agnostic (templated JSON) and prober uses a short time budget so overall CI latency should improve for typical PRs.
